title: Data Flow Attestation and Supply Chain Evidence Bundle for Private Deploys
author: Aisha Mehta
content:
Overview:

This page defines a standard evidence bundle and attestation workflow to be delivered by the field/operator team during handoff for Redwood Private deployments (VPC or on-premise). The bundle is intended to accelerate customer acceptance, provide regulatory evidence for audits, and reduce ambiguity during upgrade/rollback and day-2 operations. This is an operator-facing runbook and acceptance template, not an exhaustive compliance policy.

Scope:

- Applies to: new private installs, major upgrades (component version bumps), and control-plane migration events.
- Environments: VPC-based private control planes, air-gapped on-prem appliances, and hybrid control-plane topologies.
- Audience: Field engineers, customer SREs, solutions engineering, and compliance owners.

Why this bundle exists:

1) Provide a repeatable set of artifacts customers and auditors can consume.
2) Reduce acceptance friction by mapping functional tests to evidence items.
3) Preserve chain-of-custody for software images, firmware, and cryptographic keys.

Bundle structure (artifact categories):

1) Identity & Access Evidence
- RBAC snapshot: gate-config.json (RBAC roles, service accounts, groups with timestamps).
- Auth integration proof: SSO SAML metadata or OIDC discovery endpoint plus test assertion logs sampled over a 24h window.
- KMS/HSM integration: signed export of key wrapping metadata (nonce, key id, provider, rotation epoch).

2) Software Supply Chain & Image Integrity
- Signed image manifest: container-manifest-signed.json (image digest + signature).
- SBOM: SBOM-<release>-cyclonedx.json and human-readable summary.
- Signing key attestations: CA cert chain and proof of code-signing key access controls.
- Firmware inventory: NIC and BMC firmware versions with vendor-signed checksums.

3) Network & Data Flow Proofs
- Topology diagram (PDF/PNG) annotated with private IP ranges, peering, and NACL/SG rules.
- Captured flow logs: 48-hour sampling of VPC Flow Logs (or equivalent) for control-plane-to-runtime paths.
- Proxy/MITM proof: TLS certificate pinning snapshot and tcpdump snippets demonstrating end-to-end TLS.

4) Telemetry & Observability Evidence
- Metrics snapshot: Prometheus query results (last 1h and 24h) for critical SLOs (token latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization).
- Traces: 5 example traces covering cold-start, kv-cache-hit, and model-swap path. Obfuscate customer data as required.
- Log sample bundle: 7 days (rotated) containing bootstrap, driver, and operator events with ingestion hashes.

5) Operational Runbooks & Acceptance Tests
- Acceptance test list: PASS/FAIL CSV with test IDs, short description, operator who ran them, timestamps, and artifacts produced.
- Smoke-run scripts: smoke_acceptance.sh output and logs.
- Rollback showback: pre-upgrade snapshot and rollback verification checklist.

Required metadata for every artifact:

- artifact_name: human-friendly name
- artifact_type: (evidence / snapshot / binary / SBOM / log / trace)
- produced_by: (operator/service name)
- produced_at: ISO8601 timestamp
- sha256: hex digest
- signed_by: key id / fingerprint (where applicable)

Acceptance criteria (minimal):

1) Identity & Access: RBAC snapshot has no default-allow roles assigned to service accounts, and SSO assertions are validated with no failed assertions >0 in the sampled period.
2) Image integrity: Every runtime image serving models must have a signed manifest and SBOM. Image digests in runtime match signed-manifest digests.
3) Network isolation: Control-plane and runtime planes show no unexpected egress destinations in the sampled VPC flow logs.
4) Telemetry: Critical SLOs meet thresholds for the last 24h: 95th percentile server-side token latency < 120ms, error rate < 0.5% for production traffic slice.
5) Operational: Smoke tests (end-to-end inference, model-swap, KV cache restore) pass without manual intervention.

Deliverable checklist (operator):

1) create evidence-bundle-<customer>-<date>.tar.gz containing the artifact files outlined above
2) populate evidence_manifest.json (one-line JSON summary for each artifact using the Required metadata schema above)
3) push signed bundle to customer evidence endpoint (S3 pre-signed URL or SCP to approved workstation).
4) send Handoff email with bundle link, short list of open issues, owner contacts, and proposed canary/rollout schedule.

Handoff & acceptance workflow (recommended):

1) Pre-handoff: Operator runs acceptance test suite in a staging-equivalent slice. Record PASS/FAIL and attach traces/logs.
2) Evidence upload: Operator delivers the signed evidence bundle to agreed endpoint and updates the acceptance ticket.
3) Customer validation window (48–72 hours): Customer runs their validation tests; customer may request additional artifacts.
4) Sign-off: Customer signs the acceptance PDF template; Redwood records sign-off in the project tracker and returns a signed copy.

Escalation gates and timeline:

- Gate A (Immediate): If image integrity mismatches are found, halt rollout and initiate rollback within 30 minutes.
- Gate B (24h): If telemetry SLO violations persist after 24 hours post-install, open a Severity-2 incident and engage runtime and infra oncall.
- Gate C (5 business days): If unresolved compliance questions remain, treat deployment as paused and schedule a remediation window.

Operator checklist: quick commands and examples

- Generate SBOM (example for OCI image):
  docker run --rm --privileged anchore/syft:latest syft registry.example.com/redwood/runtime:1.7.2 -o cyclonedx-json > SBOM-runtime-1.7.2.json

- Create signed image manifest (example, using cosign):
  cosign sign --key cosign.key registry.example.com/redwood/runtime@sha256:<digest>

- Produce RBAC snapshot (Kubernetes example):
  kubectl get clusterrolebinding,rolebinding --all-namespaces -o json > gate-config.json
  sha256sum gate-config.json

- Collect flow logs (AWS example):
  aws logs get-log-events --log-group-name /aws/vpc/flow-logs --start-time <t0> --end-time <t1> > vpc-flow-sample.json

Privacy and redaction guidance:

- Do not include customer raw PII or model outputs in evidence bundles. Where traces or logs contain content derived from requests, replace with deterministic placeholders and document the redaction process.
- For regulated customers, produce an additional redacted bundle and a sealed, access-controlled raw bundle for audit review only.

Chain-of-custody and signing recommendations:

- All bundles must be signed (cosign, GPG, or equivalent) with operator keys tracked in the project ledger.
- Maintain a ledger entry for each bundle: bundle-id, created_by, created_at, cosign-fingerprint, storage-location, customer-confirmation-id.

Example acceptance sign-off template (text to copy):

"We have reviewed the Data Flow Attestation and Supply Chain Evidence Bundle (bundle-id: <bundle-id>) for the private deployment in scope. The artifacts listed in evidence_manifest.json have been validated according to the acceptance criteria. We accept the environment for production traffic per the agreed SLA and notes below. Signed: <customer-sre> Date: <YYYY-MM-DD>"

Open risks and mitigations (examples):

- Risk: Intermittent firmware mismatches across identical machine SKUs. Mitigation: Quarantine nodes, reflash to vendor-provided firmware, re-capture checksums, and re-run image integrity checks.
- Risk: Late discovery of missing SBOM entries. Mitigation: Temporarily freeze rollout; require developer build to produce full SBOM and re-sign images.

Appendix A: Minimal artifact manifest example (one-line JSON per artifact)

{"artifact_name": "SBOM-runtime-1.7.2.json", "artifact_type": "SBOM", "produced_by": "operator-aws-01", "produced_at": "2027-02-10T14:03:21Z", "sha256": "af3b9c...", "signed_by": "cosign:f2c3..."}

Appendix B: Owner and escalation contacts

- Field operations (primary): field-ops@redwood.ai (oncall: +1-415-555-0182)
- Runtime & kernel team (secondary): runtime-oncall@redwood.ai (pager: +1-415-555-0110)
- Compliance review (legal): compliance@redwood.ai
